Ik Kil, a cenote on the Yucatán Peninsula, is part of an excursion route to Chichén Itzá. A stop at the pool offers a chance to explore another side of Mexico's landscape after visiting the archaeological complex.

The journey combines ancient stone structures with a natural pool. The visiting order and time spent by the water depend on the itinerary of the particular tour.

## The Ica Stones and Huacachina Oasis: What to See in Ica, Peru

### Ica — Peru's Treasure-Trove City!

Ica is a small city in southern Peru, near the Pacific coast. Yet what most visitors come here for is not a seaside holiday but a treasure trove of secrets and mysteries that have been preserved here for thousands of years.

## Discover Peru's Mysteries in Ica!

The main mystery of the Ica stones lies in the images engraved on them. Scenes scratched into their surfaces with some kind of sharp instrument depict people hunting prehistoric animals, surgical procedures, astronomers using telescopes or spyglasses, and geographical maps showing unknown continents. Some specialists call these stones the greatest discovery of the 20th century. And on a flight in a light aircraft, you can see the remarkable Nazca drawings depicting animals and human figures. Just five kilometers from Ica lies the picturesque Huacachina Oasis. It is surrounded on all sides by sand dunes, with a lake in the middle. Here you can ride boards down the sand dunes.

## The Amazon River and the Jungle: What to See in Iquitos, Peru

### Iquitos — a City on the Amazon

The charming city of Iquitos is one of Peru's most important cities on the banks of the Amazon. It still retains some of the architectural splendor of the great rubber barons of the 19th century.

## Iquitos — the Starting Point for Jungle Adventures!

From Iquitos, you can begin a journey to a variety of jungle lodges and visit Indigenous communities living in the rainforest, including the Bora and Yagua peoples. They have preserved many of their traditions. In the city, you can buy souvenirs and sample local cuisine. You can also take jungle excursions, travel along the river by boat past enchanting greenery and visit butterfly farms.

One of the youngest resorts on Mexico's Pacific coast, Ixtapa attracts visitors with its excellent conditions for a holiday.

## An Unforgettable Stay in Ixtapa and Zihuatanejo!

Ixtapa attracts travelers with a wonderful combination of sunshine, a blue sea rich in fish and coral, crystal-white beaches, high mountains and volcanoes, jungles full of exotic wildlife, and numerous restaurants. Nature is just as inviting in the nearby fishing town of Zihuatanejo. A holiday here is peaceful and idyllic. Small restaurants prepare fresh seafood dishes, and on walks toward the sheltered bay you can see many seabirds.
